 Politics MAC urges Beijing to recognize ROC's existence after Xi's remarks 
 11/12/2026 07:58 PM Listen Link Whatsapp Reddit Line Email To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below. 
 Chinese President Xi Jinping (center). CNA file photo 
 Taipei, Nov. 12 (CNA) The Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) on Thursday urged Beijing to recognize the continued existence of the Republic of China (ROC) and respect Taiwan's democracy after Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) reiterated that unification with Taiwan was inevitable.
 Xi made the remarks at a ceremony in Beijing marking what China calls the 160th anniversary of the birth of Sun Yat-sen (孫中山), who led the revolution that overthrew the Qing dynasty and established the ROC in 1912.
 Sun is revered on both sides of the Taiwan Strait for his role in ending imperial rule. The ROC government, which retreated to Taiwan in 1949 after losing the Chinese Civil War, regards him as its founding father.
 Opposition KMT holds a ceremony in honor of Sun Yat-sen. CNA file photo The People's Republic of China (PRC), meanwhile, hails Sun as a pioneer of China's democratic revolution.
 In his speech, Xi portrayed the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) as the most faithful successor to Sun's revolutionary cause, arguing that the late leader's commitment to national unity supported Beijing's goal of unification with Taiwan.
 Xi described achieving China's "complete reunification" as a historical mission of the CCP, declaring that "the tide of history cannot be stopped" and that unification "must and will be achieved."
 The Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China. CNA file photo He also reiterated Beijing's commitment to "peaceful reunification" under its "one country, two systems" framework, saying China was willing to hold talks on cross-strait relations and unification while insisting that there would be no room for Taiwan independence.
 "One country, two systems" is a framework Beijing has implemented in Hong Kong and Macao following their handovers from British and Portuguese rule, respectively, and proposed for Taiwan, but both Taiwan's government and a majority of its people have rejected it.
 MAC's response
 In a statement issued after its regular news briefing, MAC accused Beijing of distorting historical narratives and using Sun's legacy to promote unification with Taiwan.
 "If the CCP truly wishes to commemorate Sun Yat-sen, it should acknowledge the objective fact that the ROC he founded continues to exist," the council said, calling on Beijing to respect Taiwan's democratic way of life and pursue political reform.
 The council said the ROC had never been overthrown or replaced, and that neither it nor the PRC was subordinate to the other.
 "The PRC has never ruled Taiwan for a single day," MAC said, arguing that Beijing had no right to impose unification on Taiwan or determine its future.
 CNA file photo It also rejected "one country, two systems," saying Taiwan's future should be decided by its 23 million people under the ROC's democratic constitutional system.
 Earlier at the briefing, MAC deputy head and spokesperson Liang Wen-chieh (梁文傑) said Xi's remarks on unification with Taiwan were "not much different from the past."
 Liang said the speech primarily sought to portray the CCP as the legitimate successor to Sun's revolutionary ideals and bolster the legitimacy of CCP rule and Xi's political ideology.
 While Beijing described Thursday's event as marking Sun's 160th birth anniversary, Taiwan's government marked Sun's 160th birth anniversary last year and considers 2026 his 161st, following a traditional counting system that treats the year of birth as the first year.
 (By Sunny Lai)
